s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive dyspnea and joint pain in a patient with a history of rheumatic mitral stenosis and recent valve repair
salient_findings: Progressive dyspnea on exertion, orthopnea, and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and positive C-reactive protein
key_facts: 36-year-old woman with rheumatic mitral stenosis
Status post mitral valvotomy and two valve repairs
Received streptokinase for suspected prosthetic mitral valve thrombosis two weeks prior
Experienced fever and bilateral knee pain over the past 3 days
No pallor, icterus, cyanosis, edema, or jugular venous distension on examination
Joint exam showed no swelling, erythema, or warmth
Hemoglobin 9.65 g/dL, neutrophils 41%, lymphocytes 43%, platelets 4,456,000/µL
Prothrombin time 32.8 s, INR 2.5
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and positive C-reactive protein
Blood and urine cultures were sterile
Serologic tests for hepatitis B surface antigen, antinuclear antibody, anti–cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody, and lactate dehydrogenase were negative

shortlist.label: Serum Sickness
shortlist.why_kept: Recent streptokinase administration and symptoms of fever and joint pain

shortlist.label: Acute Rheumatic Fever
shortlist.why_kept: History of rheumatic mitral stenosis and presentation with fever and joint pain

shortlist.label: Prosthetic Valve Endocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Recent valve repair and presentation with fever

shortlist.label: Infective Endocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: History of valve repair and presentation with fever

shortlist.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Presentation with fever, joint pain, and elevated inflammatory markers

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of fever, bilateral knee pain, and elevated inflammatory markers (erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein) following the administration of streptokinase are consistent with serum sickness, a known adverse reaction to certain medications.

rejected.label: Acute Rheumatic Fever
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and laboratory results do not meet the Jones criteria for acute rheumatic fever.

rejected.label: Prosthetic Valve Endocarditis
rejected.why: The patient's blood and urine cultures were sterile, and there is no other evidence to suggest endocarditis.

rejected.label: Infective Endocarditis
rejected.why: The patient's blood and urine cultures were sterile, and there is no other evidence to suggest infective endocarditis.

rejected.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
rejected.why: The patient's serologic tests for antinuclear antibody and other lupus-related antibodies were negative, making this diagnosis unlikely.
